title: MIA-aware FinFlex Cell Legalization with Power-Driven Cell Version Substitution
problem: Standard cell legalization and placement optimization for TSMC FinFlex technology in sub-3nm nodes, accounting for multiple cell versions with varying heights and threshold voltages while respecting minimum implant area (MIA) constraints.
motivation: FinFlex cells provide design flexibility but complicate placement optimization due to version diversity; efficient cell substitution can improve power efficiency and area utilization in advanced nodes.
method: The algorithm uses three stages. First, it scans for violations within each row, considering both timing (speed) and power consumption. Second, it creates an initial arrangement using a directed acyclic graph (a dependency diagram showing how cells relate to each other) and selects which version of each cell to use—choosing between power-efficient and faster variants. Third, it removes violations between rows using dynamic programming (an optimization technique that builds solutions step-by-step), while ensuring manufacturing minimum implant area requirements are satisfied.
key_novelty: It's the first systematic approach to FinFlex cell legalization that combines power-driven cell version selection with minimum implant area constraint handling, using both directed acyclic graphs (dependency diagrams) and dynamic programming (an optimization technique).
contributions: First legalization algorithm for FinFlex technology addressing version substitution and MIA constraints
Multi-stage approach combining DAG-based legalization with dynamic programming for violation removal
Power efficiency optimization through intelligent cell version selection
